Article Title: 'Gave up PM post, became Super PM': BJP targets Sonia Gandhi over UPA role after memoir release
Article Text:
'Super PM' jibe at Sonia as BJP revisits her UPA role after memoir release

NEW DELHI: BJP Rajya Sabha member Sudhanshu Trivedi on Wednesday criticised senior Congress leader Sonia Gandhi over her role during the UPA government, claiming she gave up the Prime Minister's post in 2004 but went on to become a “Super PM” as chairperson of the National Advisory Council (NAC).Addressing a presser, Trivedi questioned how Sonia could decline the Prime Minister's office while holding a Cabinet minister-ranked position in the NAC, alleging that she continued to wield considerable influence over the Manmohan Singh government.“She gave up the post of Prime Minister and became a Super PM. You will not find such an example anywhere in the world, where someone gives up the post of Prime Minister but takes the rank of a Cabinet minister,” Trivedi said.He also questioned Sonia's appointment as NAC chairperson, claiming the position carried the rank of a Cabinet minister and came under the Office of Profit provisions.“She became the chairperson of the National Advisory Council (NAC), with the rank of a Cabinet minister, and that too under the Office of Profit,” he said.“I believe all these facts are before the people of the country, and everyone knows what the Super PM and Super Cabinet were during that period of governance,” Trivedi added.His remarks come amid the political debate surrounding Sonia's memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, released on Tuesday. In the book, former Congress chief recounts the circumstances that led her to decline the Prime Minister's post after the Congress-led alliance won the 2004 Lok Sabha elections.Sonia writes that she had initially ruled out becoming Prime Minister during a conversation with her children, Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra. Both had opposed her taking the position, having experienced the trauma of the assassinations of their grandmother, former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, and their father, Rajiv Gandhi .She recalls that alliance leaders subsequently pressed her to accept the post, prompting her to reluctantly say “theek hai”. However, after reflecting on the decision, she told Rahul Gandhi that she would stick to her original stand.Sonia later announced in Parliament that she would follow her “inner voice” and nominated Manmohan Singh as the Congress parliamentary party leader, paving the way for him to become Prime Minister.
Article Summary: Sudhanshu Trivedi questions Sonia Gandhi's role as chairperson of the National Advisory Council. He claims she gave up the Prime Minister's post in 2004 but went on to become a ‘Super PM’ His remarks come amid the political debate surrounding Sonia's memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love.

Article Title: 'Managing hashtags and state are different': BJP takes swipe at Vijay over alleged fund theft in Tamil Nadu
Article Text:
BJP questions Vijay govt's oversight after Rs 22.10 crore allegedly stolen from accounts

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party on Tuesday accused the Vijay-led Tamil Nadu government of administrative lapses after allegedly Rs 22.10 crore was siphoned off from government bank accounts in three districts, demanding answers from the chief minister over the incident.BJP leader Vinoj Selvam, in a post on X, alleged that Rs 14 crore was siphoned off from Ramanathapuram, Rs 3.10 crore from Nagapattinam and Rs 5 crore from Tiruppur.“Three districts. Multiple government accounts. Crores of taxpayers' money allegedly stolen!” Selvam said, raising questions over the Vijay government's financial oversight and accountability.“These are funds meant for rural development, essential services and public welfare. Money entrusted to the government for the benefit of ordinary citizens,” he wrote.The BJP leader questioned how cybercriminals allegedly breached government payment systems and executed transactions worth crores, asking where the security checks, financial controls and monitoring mechanisms were.“Where is chief minister Vijay when the people of Tamil Nadu demand answers?” Selvam said, alleging a communication gap between the chief minister, his ministers and the public.Taking a swipe at the TVK government's functioning, Selvam said political parties had IT wings, but Tamil Nadu had witnessed an actor's fan club and social media army move from trending hashtags to running a state government.“Unfortunately, managing hashtags and managing a state are two very different things,” he said.Selvam demanded transparent answers, stronger institutions and assurances that the government could safeguard public funds.
Article Summary: BJP leader Vinoj Selvam alleged that Rs 14 crore was siphoned off from Ramanathapuram, Rs 3.10 crore from Nagapattinam and Rs 5 crore from Tiruppur. “These are funds meant for rural development, essential services and public welfare. Money entrusted to the government for the benefit of ordinary citizens,” he wrote.

Article Title: 'NCP merger can't happen without us': CM Fadnavis after Sunetra-faction leaders meet Sharad Pawar
Article Text:
CM responds amid renewed speculation over a possible reunion of the two NCP

‘Unfair to compare Sunetra Pawar with

Ajit Pawar

’

NEW DELHI: Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis on Tuesday said only NCP leaders Sharad Pawar and Sunetra Pawar could clarify whether the two factions of the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) would merge, asserting that neither had discussed any such proposal with the BJP.“If they (Sharad Pawar and Sunetra Pawar) decide to merge, they will come and tell us, because the merger cannot happen without us. Neither of them has told us anything yet,” Fadnavis told reporters on the sidelines of a Diwali gathering at his official residence, Varsha, in Mumbai.The remarks come amid renewed speculation over a possible reunion of the two NCP factions after several leaders of the Sunetra Pawar-led NCP, including Praful Patel and Parth Pawar, met NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar last week.Sharad Pawar was recently hospitalised with a chest infection.Asked to compare Sunetra Pawar's leadership with that of her late husband Ajit Pawar, Fadnavis said such a comparison would be unfair, noting that Ajit Pawar had decades of political experience and a deep understanding of Maharashtra.“Ajit Dada was a leader who had been tested over time. He had an immense understanding of Maharashtra and a deep knowledge of the state.Sunetra Pawar is now adapting to the situation. Comparing her with Ajit Dada would be unfair,” he said.The chief minister added that other senior NCP leaders were collectively managing the party.Ajit Pawar, who was the deputy chief minister and NCP president, died in an air crash on January 28. Sunetra Pawar subsequently took over as the party's president and became deputy chief minister in the Mahayuti government, which comprises the BJP and Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena.
Article Summary: Devendra Fadnavis says only NCP leaders Sharad Pawar and Sunetra Pawar could clarify whether the two factions of the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) would merge. He adds that neither had discussed any such proposal with the BJP.

Article Title: From Babri to Batla House, VHP accuses Sonia of 'selective outrage'
Article Text:
From Babri to Batla House, VHP accuses Sonia of 'selective outrage'

NEW DELHI: VHP Tuesday demanded an apology from Sonia Gandhi for statements that it claimed "have hurt Hindus". VHP's Surendra Jain asked why Gandhi, who had purportedly shed tears over the demolition of the Babri structure, had not shown similar anguish when more than 350 temples were demolished and Hindus were massacred in Kashmir, Congress netas were killed by Naxalites in Bastar, or Sikhs were massacred in Delhi in 1984.Jain accused Gandhi of selective outrage, saying that she had expressed grief over the killing of terrorists in the Batla House encounter but remained silent on attacks against Hindus and the sacrifices of security personnel.He questioned whether Sonia had expressed similar grief over the death of inspector Mohan Chand Sharma, who was fatally wounded during the operation in Delhi's Batla House.He also cited the killing of Hindu tourists in Pahalgam and alleged atrocities against Hindus in Bangladesh, Pakistan, Bengal and Keralam.He further questioned Gandhi's response to the killing of kar sevaks and the 1984 anti-Sikh killings, accusing Congress of remaining indifferent to such incidents.Targeting Congress over what he described as Muslim appeasement, Jain also criticised a party leader's reported remarks contrasting pollution levels during Diwali and Eid.
Article Summary: VHP demands apology from Sonia Gandhi for statements that it claimed "have hurt Hindus" VHP's Surendra Jain asked why Gandhi had purportedly shed tears over the demolition of the Babri structure. He also questioned whether Sonia had expressed similar grief over the death of inspector Mohan Chand Sharma.

Article Title: 'Babar premis will be punished': BJP targets TMC's Kirti Azad over Ram Mandir remarks
Article Text:
“Babar Premis will be punished by people of Uttar Pradesh just like Bengal,” Bhandari wrote.

NEW DELHI: BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari on Wednesday criticised Trinamool Congress TMC ) MP Kirti Azad over his remarks on Lord Ram and the Ayodhya Ram Mandir , accusing the opposition of engaging in “peak vote bank politics”.In a post on X, Bhandari accused the TMC of insulting Lord Ram and alleged that the Congress-led INDIA bloc was opposed to Sanatan.“Congress lead Opposition hates Sanatan! TMC MP insults Prabhu Shree Ram! By asking their leaders to continue to slander Sanatan Rahul Gandhi, Mamta Banerjee and Akhilesh Yadav are practising 'Peak vote bank politics'.He also warned that opposition parties would face punishment in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, similar to the TMC's electoral defeat in West Bengal.“Babar Premis will be punished by people of Uttar Pradesh just like Bengal,” Bhandari wrote.The BJP leader's remarks came after Azad said he would never visit the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya, questioning the treatment of Maa Sita by Lord Ram.Speaking to news agency ANI, the TMC MP said he did not consider Lord Ram the only deity worthy of worship and referred to Maa Sita as his mother, saying he belonged to her birthplace, Mithila.“Is Lord Ram the only God among the 3,200 crore deities in our country? I will never go there because Lord Ram abandoned his wife, even after she had passed the Agni Pariksha and sent Maa Sita away from his home,” he said.“Why should I go? I belong to the birthplace of Maa Sita. She was the daughter of Mithila. Maa Sita is my mother. For every person belonging to Mithila, Maa Sita is a mother,” he added.Azad questioned the description of Lord Ram as “Maryada Purushottam” and said he worshipped Maa Kali. He also named temples he visits, including Kamakhya, Dakshina Kali, Kalighat and the Kali Temple at Gol Market in Delhi.“Does that mean I am not a Hindu?” he asked.The row erupted ahead of Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav's proposed visit to the Ram Mandir in December, ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections.
Article Summary: Kirti Azad said he would never visit the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya, questioning the treatment of Maa Sita by Lord Ram. Bhandari accused the TMC of insulting Lord Ram and alleged that the Congress-led INDIA bloc was opposed to Sanatan. He also warned that opposition parties would face punishment in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.

Article Title: EC: Code of conduct applies to retd govt officials in state jobs
Article Text:
EC: Code of conduct applies to retd govt officials in state jobs

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: EC Tuesday directed that the "political neutrality" provision of model code of conduct (MCC) will henceforth apply not just to serving govt employees in poll-bound states but also to retired govt officials and staffers attached, employed or re-employed by state govts.As per relevant MCC instructions, govt employees, and now retired or re-employed officers, "are not expected to take part in any election campaign or canvassing and should take scrupulous care not to lend their names, official position or authority to assist one individual/political party/group against another".MCC provisions apply to all organisations, committees, corporations and commissions funded wholly or partially by govt, and their employees. Relevant conduct rules in states also prohibit govt servants from taking part in political activities and elections.EC directed that retired and re-employed officials and staffers will, during the MCC period, not summon any election-related officer of the constituency or district where polls have been announced for official meetings, or hold video conferences with them. Any violation of the directions "shall be viewed seriously", it said in a letter to chief secretaries and CEO of five poll-bound states - UP, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Goa and Manipur Until now, there were no guidelines on political neutrality and conduct of retired officials attached or re-employed by states during MCC period. Some are attached to or re-employed by the offices of CMs and ministers.
Article Summary: EC: Code of conduct applies to retd govt officials in state jobs. Relevant conduct rules in states also prohibit govt servants from taking part in political activities and elections. Until now, there were no guidelines on political neutrality and conduct of retired officials attached or re-employed by states.

Article Title: 'Tipu fought 4 Anglo-Mysore wars; RSS skipped freedom struggle': Karnataka minister Priyank Kharge

NEW DELHI: Karnataka home minister Priyank Kharge on Tuesday defended Tipu Sultan , saying that while the former Mysore ruler fought four Anglo-Mysore Wars, the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) had "no role in India's freedom struggle.""The BJP needs to get its history right. Tipu Sultan fought four Anglo-Mysore Wars. The RSS did not even participate in the freedom struggle. They did not take part in the Civil Disobedience Movement, Quit India Movement, Dandi March or Non-Cooperation Movement, nor were they involved in any of the Round Table Conferences. They did nothing, yet they are the ones dictating terms," Priyank Kharge, son of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, told reporters.The RSS is the ideological mentor of the BJP, which is the principal opposition party in Karnataka and has been India's governing party since 2014.The Congress leader also cited a book in which senior BJP leader and former Karnataka chief minister BS Yediyurappa had praised Tipu Sultan, accusing the BJP of engaging in "pure opportunistic politics". Priyank Kharge alleged that the saffron party adopts a pro-minority stance while seeking votes but changes its position after elections."The BJP opposed Tipu Jayanti when Yediyurappa ji was the chief minister, yet he had praised Tipu Sultan in a book. You cannot erase Tipu Sultan's contributions to the state. This is nothing but politics. When they want votes, they become pro-minority; when they don't, they behave differently. The government will take a decision. You cannot simply erase history, whether you like it or not," he added.His remarks came after cultural organisation Tehrik-e-Khudadad submitted a memorandum to Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar, urging the state government to reinstate the official celebration of Tipu Sultan Jayanti on November 10.The organisation also called on the authorities to review school textbooks to ensure that Tipu Sultan and his father, Hyder Ali, receive what it described as "historically accurate" coverage.The proposal is currently pending before the Chief Minister's Office.Tipu Sultan Jayanti was first introduced in 2015 by the Congress government led by then chief minister Siddaramaiah. However, the celebration was discontinued in 2019 by the-then BJP-led government.
Article Summary: Karnataka home minister Priyank Kharge defends Tipu Sultan. He says the former Mysore ruler fought four Anglo-Mysore Wars. Kharge says the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh had "no role in India's freedom struggle"

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke in another X post on Monday claimed that the local Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) in his hometown had “suddenly gone on leave” and that a new officer had been brought in to take charge.Dipke’s remarks came amid party's earlier claim that he and fellow CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Dass could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other provisions.AISA national president Neha Bora on Monday claimed that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station.In a post on X, Neha said "Rosy and other protesting journalists are detained at Delhi Cantt PS. Team of lawyer comrades are in touch with them.But if any lawyer can be at the PS immediately, pls DM."Rosie is among the three female journalists who filed complaint alleging sexual harassment by police personnel during a protest in the New Delhi area on October 3.The complants have been transferred to the Crime Branch at Kamla Market for further action.Delhi Police also detained several protesters outside Parliament Street Police Station who were demonstrating over an alleged incident of sexual misconduct involving three women journalists during an October 3 protest at Jantar Mantar.The protesters alleged that they had been demonstrating since 6pm on Sunday, demanding registration of an FIR in the case. Police detained them around 7am on Monday following a clash, with protesters alleging they were treated poorly despite only seeking registration of an FIR. Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Derek O’Brien also extended support to Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders as party spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka claimed that multiple sources had warned that the three could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other equivalent provisions.“With you all the way 🪳🪳stay strong. ‘10 Oct poora desh aa raha hai…’,” O’Brien said in a post on X while replying to Dipke.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacting to the claim said they would not be intimidated by the possibility of action under laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) or National Security Act (NSA).“If the Govt believes that the threat of UAPA, NSA or years behind bars will scare us into silence, it won’t,” Dipke said in a post on X, adding that the protesters were prepared to spend “months or years in jail” but would not back down from their campaign to “save democracy”.He further said that they follow the path shown by Mahatma Gandhi and continue to resist “peacefully and non-violently”, despite what he described as attempts by the state to intimidate them.The developments come amid the CJP-led campaign against the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The protesters have been demanding accountability from chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the exercise and have announced further mobilisation on October 10 in Delhi.
Article Summary: AISA national president Neha Bora claims that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station. Article Title: Diwali crackers cure several diseases, says BJP MLA Papia Adhikari during Kali Puja
Article Text:
BJP’s Tollygunge MLA Papia Adhikari





KOLKATA: Days after chief minister Suvendu Adhikari issued a special message on bursting loud firecrackers during Kali Puja and Diwali celebrations, BJP ’s Tollygunge MLA Papia Adhikari claimed that bursting firecrackers can cure several diseases.Papia Adhikari, the MLA from Tollygunge, had gone to inaugurate a Kali Puja in her constituency.As she began speaking with a microphone in hand, a firecracker went off loudly in front of her. Continuing with her speech, she said, “You will see that bursting firecrackers will cure several diseases.”“Our chief minister has said that we will burst firecrackers. How can Kali Puja be complete without firecrackers? We will definitely burst firecrackers. However, we will follow the guidelines by the police,” she said.Earlier, speaking at the inaugural stages of several Kali Puja pandals, including those at Amherst Street and Khalishani, the CM said that firecrackers will be burst during the festival.However, he urged everyone to ensure that eco-friendly or green crackers are used and that noise pollution regulations are followed.
Article Summary: Papia Adhikari, the MLA from Tollygunge, had gone to inaugurate a Kali Puja in her constituency. As she began speaking with a microphone in hand, a firecracker went off loudly in front of her. “You will see that bursting firecrackers will cure several diseases”

Article Title: DMK MLA Durai Chandrasekar booked over remarks against Tamil Nadu CM Vijay, minister; summoned for police inquiry
Article Text:
Kilpauk police filed a case against Thiruvaiyaru DMK MLA Durai Chandrasekar regarding his comments on CM C Joseph Vijay (Durai Chandrasekar/@Facebook)





CHENNAI: Kilpauk police registered a case against Thiruvaiyaru DMK MLA Durai Chandrasekar over remarks he made against Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay and industries minister Keerthana in August.Police summoned him to appear for an inquiry at the office of the deputy commissioner of police in Kilpauk on Wednesday.According to police sources, the case was registered following complaints over the MLA's remarks about the chief minister and the minister.Following the registration of the case, Kilpauk police served a summons directing Chandrasekar to appear in person before the deputy commissioner of police on Wednesday morning.The police will question him about the remarks and record his explanation as part of the investigation.Chandrasekar was expected to appear in response to the summons along with his lawyer.
Article Summary: Kilpauk police filed a case against Thiruvaiyaru DMK MLA Durai Chandrasekar. The case was registered following complaints over the MLA's remarks about the chief minister and the minister. Police will question him about the remarks and record his explanation as part of the investigation.

Article Title: Juvenile held for ‘fake’ takedown notices to X
Article Text: New Delhi: Delhi Police is learnt to have apprehended a juvenile in connection with the case of alleged fraudulent notices sent to social media platform X, asking it to block the accounts of Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF) and Software Freedom Law Centre (SFLC).The suspect, a Class-XII student, was detained from Srinagar and produced before Juvenile Justice Board, sources said. Police didn’t disclose the motive behind the act.The crime branch of Delhi Police had filed an FIR for forgery and impersonation, and begun investigation even as X informed Delhi High Court that the takedown notices were sent by “some impostor, and not by Delhi Police”.X earlier issued notices to IFF and SFLC stating that a communication signed by special commissioner HGS Dhaliwal had sought the takedown. The alleged notices mentioned that the posts were defamatory towards RSS .
Article Summary: The suspect, a Class-XII student, was detained from Srinagar and produced before Juvenile Justice Board. The crime branch of Delhi Police had filed an FIR for forgery and impersonation. The alleged notices mentioned that the posts were defamatory towards RSS.

Article Title: 4 govt directors help BJP-led group win Kolhapur's Gokul polls; another form of vote and election chori, says Congress
Article Text:
Maharashtra’s BJP-led Mahayuti alliance secured victory in the Gokul Dairy chief election held recently





KOLHAPUR: Maharashtra ’s governing BJP-led Mahayuti alliance snatched Tuesday a win over Congress-backed group Samavichari Aghadi in a high-stakes election for Kolhapur-based Gokul Dairy’s chief, riding on the support of four new govt nominees.Mahayuti candidate, ex-NCP MLA Rajesh Patil, was elected chief after securing 16 votes, three more than his Samavichari rival Patil Chuyekar’s 13.Gokul has a 25-member board of directors, for which elections were held last month. Mahayuti had won 12 posts and Samavichari 13. Neither had the quorum of 14 required for the chief’s election.Mahayuti govt had last week promulgated an ordinance to nominate five members to large cooperatives, four with voting rights.This drew flak from the opposition, which accused govt of attempting to grab Gokul, the state’s largest milk co-operative. Congress LS leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi alleged “adulteration” of the mandate. A Samavichari plea in Bombay HC against the ordinance was rejected Monday.“We have nominated individuals with experience. If one is a gynaecologist, what’s wrong? When the country’s leader of opposition feels the need to intervene in a milk union election, a gynaecologist is just a common citizen,” CM Devendra Fadnavis said on Tuesday.Congress general secretary KC Venugopal denounced the outcome as “another form of vote and election chori”.
Article Summary: BJP-led Mahayuti alliance snatched a win over Congress-backed group Samavichari Aghadi in a high-stakes election for Kolhapur-based Gokul Dairy’s chief. Rajesh Patil, ex-NCP MLA, was elected chief after securing 16 votes.

Article Title: 40,000 farmers join protest march over Gokul poll row in Kolhapur
Article Text:
Over 40,000 individuals participated in the 'Sangharsh Morcha' march to protest against the Gokul chairperson election.





KOLHAPUR: Over 40,000 people across Kolhapur district have joined the 'Sangharsh Morcha' march onto the Kolhapur district collectorate over the ongoing row over Gokul chairperson election. Farmers' leader former MP Raju Shetti, Kolhapur MP Shahu Chhatrapati, Sangli MP Vishal Patil, MP Dhairyasheel Mohite - Patil have joined thousands of dairy farmers in the protest march that began from Dasara Chowk.The march has been called after Maharashtra govt promulgated an ordinance to nominate five members to large co-op societies, granting four of them voting rights.This is likely to impact the Gokul chairperson election that is stuck due to lack of quorum. On Monday, people from Kolhapur and adjoining districts of Sangli and Satara also joined the march.
Article Summary: The march has been called after Maharashtra govt promulgated an ordinance to nominate five members to large co-op societies. Farmers' leader former MP Raju Shetti, Kolhapur MP Shahu Chhatrapati, Sangli MP Vishal Patil, MP Dhairyasheel Mohite - Patil have joined thousands of dairy farmers.

Article Title: Cong-backed panel challenges ordinance to appoint govt-nominated members with voting rights to large co-ops in Bombay HC
Article Text:
HC Kolhapur bench

Kolhapur:





The Samavichari Aghadi panel, winning 13 directors’ posts in the Gokul dairy election, on Sunday challenged in Bombay high court’s Kolhapur bench the “constitutional validity” of the ordinance promulgated on Friday allowing state govt to appoint four members to large cooperatives of federal nature with voting rights.Confirming the development, Congress MLC Satej Patil , backing the Samavichari Aghadi, said they had sought directions that the ordinance be scrapped.Three directors elected through the Mahayuti panel have also approached the high court’s Kolhapur bench on Sunday claiming that they had not received notices regarding the petition filed in Kolhapur bench of the Bombay high court regarding a Oct 29 meeting. Both matters would be heard on Monday before the vacation bench of the high court.The election to the chairperson post of Gokul, a Rs 3,000-crore cooperative dairy in Maharashtra, is stuck as Mahayuti alliance won 12 posts and Samavichari Aghadi won 13, both not meeting the quorum required for the election of 14 in the 25-member body. The next meeting to elect the chairperson is scheduled for Nov 10 following interim directions of the Bombay high court.BJP MP Dhananjay Mahadik said, “The meeting on Oct 29 to elect the chairperson was adjourned because of the lack of a quorum.When Samavichari Aghadi moved a petition in the high court against this, the court ordered notices to be issued to 12 directors of Mahayuti regarding the petition. During the hearing on Nov 2, the opposition counsel submitted an affidavit to the court stating that all directors had received the notices. However, in reality, three directors — Ambarishsingh Ghatge, Virendra Mandlik and Karansinha Gaikwad — did not receive any notice. Therefore, they have submitted their own affidavits in the high court and filed a criminal and contempt petition.”Earlier, Maharashtra govt on Friday promulgated an ordinance to amend the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act, 1960, to appoint five govt-nominated members to the boards of federal cooperative societies with an annual turnover exceeding Rs500 crore and granted four of them voting rights. The move comes amid the ongoing logjam over the election to the chairperson post of Gokul dairy.
Article Summary: The Samavichari Aghadi panel, winning 13 directors’ posts in the Gokul dairy election, on Sunday challenged in Bombay high court’s Kolhapur bench the “constitutional validity” of the ordinance promulgated on Friday. Congress MLC Satej Patil said they had sought directions that the ordinance be scrapped. Both matters would be heard on Monday before the vacation bench of the high court. The election to the chairperson post of the Rs 3,000-crore cooperative dairy is stuck as Mahayuti alliance won 12 posts.

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Article Title: Man in Mahindra Thar with duplicate plate molests woman, knocks down another in Kharghar
Article Text:
30-year-old man was apprehended for allegedly molesting a woman and injuring another in Navi Mumbai.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team within 10 hours on Thursday evening.He had allegedly molested a 26-year-old woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night and, an hour later, severely injured a 22-year-old woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, Kharghar.Acting on a complaint by the woman allegedly molested by the Thar SUV driver, Kharghar police registered an FIR under BNS section 74 for the offence of assault or criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty.While, as per the complaint by the injured woman Shrawani Dandekar, a resident of sector 3, Belpada, an FIR under relevant BNS sections and Motor Vehicle Act was registered against the Thar SUV driver for rash and negligent driving causing hurt.The detained aaccused identified as Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of sector 50, Seawoods, Nerul was handed over to Kharghar police for further legal action.Previously, in January 2021, he was arrested by Nerul police in the FIR registered against him for alleged kidnapping, sexual harassment and molestation of a woman.Sanjay Joshi, senior inspector of Kharghar said, "The accused Nakhvi has been detained and subsequently it will be decided whether to arrest him or serve with a notice under Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) for cooperating in police investigating."Audumbar Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-3 said, "After an FIR for molestation was registered at Kharghar police station by the victim woman, a resident of sector 34, Kharghar. As per the orders of higher authority, our team started a parallel probe. From the CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we obtained the red Thar SUV's registration number, which was of Vashi RTO passing.""When verified, the registration number was found to be that of a Maruti WagonR car. As the accused had used a duplicate registration number plate, we scrutinized as many as 62 Thar SUVs registered with various Regional Transport Offices (RTOs). Subsequently, we obtained the registration number of a red Thar SUV that was registered with Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar RTO," Patil added.SPI Patil further informed, "The SUV was registered in the name of Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of Devaki Apartment in sector-50, Seawoods. From his mobile number registered with the RTO, his location was tracked.""He was apprehended from Bonkode village, Koparkhairane on Thursday late evening. Upon thorough interrogation, he confessed that he had inappropriately touched the woman pedestrian near Pethpada metro station while he drove his Thar SUV and sped away. He even confessed to have injured a woman pedestrian by hitting her his SUV while driving in Belpada area," he said.
Article Summary: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team on Thursday evening. He had allegedly molested a woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night. An hour later, he severely injured a woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, KharGHar.

Article Title: Man stabbed to death by woman's father over relationship in Perambur
Article Text: CHENNAI: A 33-year-old autorickshaw driver was stabbed to death by a man over the relationship with his daughter at the victim’s residence in Chakkarapani Thottam on Paper Mills Road in Perambur on Tuesday night. Sembium police arrested the 53-year-old accused, identified as Babu.The deceased, Ramesh, lived separately from his wife, Sharmila, and had been in a relationship with Gayathri, 31, Babu's daughter, for the past seven months. Babu had objected to their relationship, but the two continued to meet, police said.According to police, Babu went to Ramesh's house around 9pm on Tuesday. Both men were under the influence of alcohol when an argument broke out.During the altercation, Babu took a concealed blade from a nail clipper and stabbed Ramesh in the area between his left collarbone and neck before fleeing.After a while, Ramesh's grandmother, Palaniyammal, found him dead and alerted neighbours, who informed the police. Inspector Gopal of Sembium police station recovered the body and sent it to Kilpauk Medical College Hospital for postmortem examination.Police registered a murder case and arrested Babu on murder charges. He was produced before a magistrate court on Wednesday and remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: Autorickshaw driver was stabbed to death by a man over the relationship with his daughter. The deceased, Ramesh, lived separately from his wife, Sharmila, and had been in a relationship with Gayathri, 31, Babu's daughter. Babu had objected to their relationship, but the two continued to meet.

Article Title: Man dies after four-member gang attacks him with a knife in Chennai's RA Puram
Article Text:
Police arrested all four accused within hours and upgraded the case from attempted murder to murder (Representative image)





CHENNAI: A 27-year-old autorickshaw driver died after four men attacked him with a knife near the U-turn on Ramakrishna Mutt Road in Raja Annamalaipuram on Tuesday evening. Abiramapuram police arrested all four suspects within hours and altered the case from attempted murder to murder.The deceased, Sivakumar , son of Ayyappan, lived in KVB Garden in Raja Annamalaipuram. He was sitting inside his autorickshaw when the four men, who arrived on two-wheelers, attacked him and fled.Sivakumar was initially admitted to Govt Royapettah Hospital. As his condition required further treatment, he was shifted to Rajiv Gandhi Govt General Hospital, where he later succumbed to his injuries.Based on a complaint lodged by his mother, Abiramapuram police registered a case. The arrested suspects were identified as Loganathan, Veera , Ajith and Ramu Preliminary investigations revealed that Sivakumar and Loganathan had a previous enmity following a physical altercation about three years ago. Police suspected that Loganathan had carried out the attack with the help of his associates.All the four arrested men were produced before a magistrate court and remanded in judicial custody on Wednesday.
Article Summary: 27-year-old autorickshaw driver died after four men attacked him with a knife. Police arrested all four suspects within hours and upgraded the case from attempted murder to murder. The arrested suspects were identified as Loganathan, Veera, Ajith and Ramu.

Article Title: 23 sovereigns of gold jewellery stolen from house in Coimbatore
Article Text: COIMBATORE: Unidentified people stole 23 sovereigns of gold jewellery from a house at Akshaya Orbit Apartments in Sundaresan Iyer Layout on the Trichy Road here.The complainant, S Deepa, 52, attended a relative’s wedding on Oct 29 wearing gold jewellery. Around 7am on Oct 30, she returned home, removed the jewellery and kept it in a cupboard in her bedroom.Around 6.30pm on Nov 7, while checking the jewellery before leaving for her mother’s house, she found that 23 sovereigns of gold ornaments were missing. The stolen jewellery included eight bangles weighing 12 sovereigns, two pairs of earrings weighing four sovereigns, a bracelet weighing two sovereigns, a pair of cuffs weighing two sovereigns and a chain weighing three sovereigns.She lodged a complaint with the Race Course police on Sunday. Police registered a case under Section 305(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and began an investigation. Police visited the house and collected evidence. They have taken fingerprints and CCTV footage for further investigations.
Article Summary: The complainant, S Deepa, 52, attended a relative’s wedding on Oct 29 wearing gold jewellery. Around 7am on Oct 30, she returned home, removed the jewellery and kept it in a cupboard in her bedroom. Around 6.30pm on Nov 7, she found that 23 sovereigns of gold ornaments were missing.

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.
Article Summary: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district. Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid.

Article Title: Cop suspended over woman’s plaint of house trespass, sexual harassment
Article Text:
Cop suspended over woman’s plaint of house trespass, sexual harassment





Tuticorin: A special branch head constable of Tharuvaikulam police station in Tuticorin district has been placed under suspension after a woman accused him of trespassing into her house and making obscene and sexually suggestive gestures while purportedly enquiring about her brother.A case was registered against Selvin Raja, 37, based on a complaint from the victim. The woman alleged that Raja visited her residence on Oct 27 and Nov 2 under the pretext of inquiring about her brother, who was reportedly involved in a matrimonial dispute. On Nov 6, when she was alone at home, the constable entered the premises and behaved in an obscene manner, making sexually suggestive gestures and stating that he had come specifically to see and speak with her, she said.The complainant alleged that when she questioned his repeated visits and raised an alarm, the constable fled. She immediately alerted police and later lodged a formal complaint. Subsequently, DSP M Sundarapandiyan conducted an inquiry with both the complainant and the accused. Based on the findings, police registered a case for house-trespass, sexual harassment and action intended to insult the modesty of a woman under BNS, and Section 4 (harassment of women) of Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act.Police said a notice was served on the accused, and departmental action also initiated. Selvin Raja was placed under suspension on Nov 7, and further investigation was underway.
Article Summary: A case was registered against Selvin Raja, 37, based on a complaint from the victim. The woman alleged that Raja visited her residence on Oct 27 and Nov 2 under the pretext of inquiring about her brother. Raja was placed under suspension on Nov 7, and further investigation was underway.

Article Title: Three die as bikes collide head-on near Melur
Article Text:
Three die as bikes collide head-on near Melur

Madurai:





A Diwali morning trip to buy meat turned tragic after two motorcycles collided head-on near Melur in Madurai district on Sunday, leaving three people, including a father and his son, dead on the spot. Police said the accident occurred on the Alagarkovil Road when two motorcycles travelling in opposite directions crashed into each other. The impact was so severe that Arumugam and his son Lokesh of Othakadai, who were travelling on one of the two-wheelers, died on the spot. Naveen , who was riding the other two-wheeler, also succumbed to his injuries. Melur police rushed to the spot and shifted the bodies to the Melur govt hospital for postmortem examination. A case has been registered.
Article Summary: A Diwali morning trip to buy meat turned tragic after two motorcycles collided head-on near Melur in Madurai district on Sunday. Police said the accident occurred on the Alagarkovil Road when two motorcycles travelling in opposite directions crashed into each other. The impact was so severe that Arumugam and his son Lokesh of Othakadai, who were travelling on one of the two-wheelers, died on the spot.

Article Title: Retired govt employee trampled to death by elephant
Article Text:
Subbaiah who was trampled to death by a wild elephant at Puliyarai in Tenkasi district

Madurai:





A retired highways department employee was trampled to death by a wild elephant at his coconut grove near Sengottai on Monday. This triggered a protest by villagers who prevented officials from removing his body, accusing the forest department of ignoring repeated warnings.The deceased, Subbaiah Pillai, 68, of Therkkumedu in Puliyarai, had visited his grove at Kottavikulam, behind the Dakshinamurthy temple, around 9am. An elephant chased and trampled him, killing him on the spot.Relatives and villagers who gathered at the spot confronted forest and police personnel when they attempted to retrieve the body. They subsequently held a road blockade, disrupting traffic.The protesters alleged that elephant movement had increased in Puliyarai and surrounding agricultural areas, but repeated complaints seeking preventive measures had gone unheeded.Senior police and forest officials held talks with the protesters and assured them of action. The blockade was withdrawn and the body was sent to Sengottai govt hospital for postmortem after noon.Meanwhile, Kadayanallur DMK MLA T M Rajendran submitted a memorandum to Tenkasi collector Monika Rana, seeking immediate compensation for the family and effective measures to prevent elephants and gaurs from entering agricultural fields.
Article Summary: The deceased, Subbaiah Pillai, 68, of Therkkumedu in Puliyarai, had visited his grove at Kottavikulam, behind the Dakshinamurthy temple, around 9am. An elephant chased and trampled him, killing him on the spot.

Article Title: Murder suspect arrested near Krishnagiri
Article Text: KRISHNAGIRI: The Krishnagiri district police on Saturday arrested a man on charges of murdering a 70- year-old woman in Pannandur village.District superintendent of police GS Anitha said, Chamundeeswari, who was living alone, was found dead under suspicious circumstances in her house on Friday morning.During investigations, police found that Suryakumar alias Surya,30, of the same village entered Chamundeeswari’s house around 1am on Friday with an intention to steal valuables. “Acting on the findings, special police teams launched a search operation and arrested the man within 12 hours of the crime,” the SP said.
Article Summary: Chamundeeswari, who was living alone, was found dead under suspicious circumstances in her house on Friday morning. Police found that Suryakumar alias Surya,30, of the same village entered the house with an intention to steal valuables.

Article Title: Cops attacked in two separate incidents in Kochi
Article Text:
Kochi

:





Police officers were attacked in two separate incidents in Kochi city on Tuesday.In the first case, a 25-year-old man bit the hand of an officer on general hospital premises early on Tuesday.The accused is Muhammad Iqbal of Sasthamkotta, Kollam. He was taken into custody on Monday night by Ernakulam Town North police for allegedly creating a disturbance on the road near North Railway Overbridge. After creating a ruckus at the police station, he was taken to hospital for a medical examination.As soon as the police vehicle reached the hospital compound, the accused, who was seated in the rear seat, jumped into the middle seat and attempted to flee. A police officer, Ajith Paul, prevented him from escaping. In the melee, the accused bit the left hand of the officer.The Ernakulam North police registered a case against Iqbal for creating a public disturbance, while the Central police booked him for allegedly biting the police officer and obstructing him from discharging his duty.Videos of Iqbal creating a commotion at the police station and verbally abusing police personnel have surfaced.During the tirade, he is also heard introducing himself, saying, “My name is Muhammad Iqbal.”Blood and other samples have been sent for examination to determine whether Iqbal was under the influence of drugs. He has been remanded in judicial custody.Meanwhile, a sub-inspector with the Kadavanthara police was attacked at Indira Gandhi co-op hospital. A police team approached the accused, Ajmal S K, 32, after finding him to be exhibiting allegedly violent behaviour. The man allegedly punched the SI on the chest and grabbed the officer’s uniform.
Article Summary: Police officers were attacked in two separate incidents in Kochi city on Tuesday. In the first case, a 25-year-old man bit the hand of an officer on general hospital premises. A sub-inspector with the Kadavanthara police was attacked at Indira Gandhi co-op hospital.

Article Title: Rape complaint: Court directs cops to file counter affidavit on doc’s anticipatory bail plea
Article Text:
Representational AI-image

Kochi

:





Ernakulam district and sessions court on Tuesday directed the police to file a counter-affidavit to the anticipatory bail plea filed by Johnson Varghese, accused of allegedly raping a 50-year-old woman. The court is likely to consider the petition this week.Three individuals, including two actors, were earlier arrested on the complaint of the doctor who accused them of assaulting him and robbing him. The rape case was filed by one of the relatives of these accused who also produced the phone, purportedly belonging to the doctor. The doctor went incommunicado soon after the complaint was filed and a lookout circular was issued against him.According to sources, Johnson is taking a stand that the rape complaint was fabricated to counter the complaint he filed against the actors.Meanwhile, the police on Tuesday conducted evidence collection against three accused persons, including the actors. They were taken to the flat in Ponnurunni where the alleged assault occurred.Kadavanthra police are investigating the robbery case while Infopark police are probing the sexual assault case.Police said that a detailed statement of the complainant in the sexual assault case will be recorded with regard to how she came into possession of the doctor’s phone.The doctor’s complaint was that the trio was part of a 12-member gang which attacked him at the flat. He alleged that he was called to the flat on the pretext that a relative of one of the accused was unwell and needed urgent medical attention. He had claimed in his complaint that the group then accused him of administering intoxicants and sexually assaulting the woman. He alleged that an attempt was made to demand money from him for not making it public.
Article Summary: Johnson Varghese is accused of allegedly raping a 50-year-old woman. Three individuals, including two actors, were earlier arrested on the complaint of the doctor who accused them of assaulting him and robbing him. The doctor went incommunicado soon after the complaint was filed and a lookout circular was issued against him.

Article Title: Fake notices in Delhi Police's name sent to X to block 2 accounts, FIR registered
Article Text:
X flags forged police communications during Delhi HC hearing; probe launched to trace those behind fake notices

NEW DELHI: The Delhi Police has registered an FIR against unidentified persons for allegedly impersonating the force and forging a senior officer's signature to send fake notices to social media platform X, seeking the blocking of two organisations' accounts.The matter surfaced during a hearing before the Delhi high court on November 6, when X informed the court that its internal investigation had found the notices, purportedly issued in the name of the Delhi Police, to be forged, news agency PTI reported.According to the platform, an unidentified person had fraudulently used the police's identity to seek the blocking of accounts belonging to the Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF) and the Software Freedom Law Centre.X clarified that it had neither taken down nor blocked the accounts based on the purported notices.Following the disclosure, the Delhi Police's Crime Branch registered an FIR against unknown persons and launched an investigation to identify those behind the forged communications, officials said. Further investigation is underway.
Article Summary: The Delhi Police has registered an FIR against unidentified persons for allegedly impersonating the force and forging a senior officer's signature. The matter surfaced during a hearing before the Delhi high court on November 6. X informed the court that its internal investigation had found the notices, purportedly issued in the name of the Delhi Police, to be forged.
